text: This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of Moab, and for four, I will not relent — because they burned the bones of the king of Edom to lime.

versions.text: This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of Moab, and for four, I will not relent — because he burned the bones of the king of Edom to lime.
versions.explanation: The translation shifts from "he" for Moab in verse 1 to "her" in verse 3, which is confusing when read aloud. Using a consistent reference ("they" for the nation, as with Judah and Israel in verses 4 and 6) removes the jarring gender shift while preserving the sense.

text: So I will send fire against Moab, and it will devour the fortresses of Kerioth. Moab will die amid the uproar, amid war cries and the blast of the ram's horn.

versions.text: So I will send fire against Moab, and it will devour the fortresses of Kerioth. Moab will die amid the uproar, amid war cries and the blast of the trumpet.
versions.explanation: The shofar is a ram's horn rather than a metal trumpet; the more precise rendering preserves the battle imagery and avoids anachronism, and it reads naturally aloud.

text: I will cut off the judge from her midst, and kill all her officials with him, declares the LORD.

versions.text: I will cut off her ruler from her midst, and kill all her officials with him, says the LORD.
versions.explanation: שׁוֹפֵט is specifically the "judge" (the one who renders judgment), a nuance lost in the generic "ruler." Also, אָמַר יְהוָה here closes the oracle; rendering it "declares the LORD" matches the formula used in verses 11 and 16 and keeps the refrain consistent for oral reading.

text: This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of Judah, and for four, I will not relent — because they rejected the law of the LORD and did not keep his statutes, and their lies led them astray, the same lies their fathers followed.
So I will send fire against Judah, and it will devour the fortresses of Jerusalem.
This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not relent — because they sell the righteous for silver, and the needy for a pair of sandals.
They trample the heads of the poor into the dust of the earth and push the humble out of the way. Father and son go in to the same young woman, and so profane my holy name.

versions.text: They trample the heads of the poor into the dust of the earth and push the humble out of the way. Father and son go in to the same girl, and so profane my holy name.
versions.explanation: Hebrew נַעֲרָה denotes a young woman of marriageable age; in modern English "girl" can suggest a child, which introduces a connotation not present in the text. "Young woman" is more accurate and reads just as smoothly aloud.

text: They stretch out beside every altar on garments taken in pledge, and in the house of their God they drink wine bought with fines.
Yet it was I who destroyed the Amorite before them, though he was as tall as the cedars and as strong as the oaks. I destroyed his fruit above and his roots below.
It was I who brought you up out of the land of Egypt and led you forty years through the wilderness, to take possession of the land of the Amorite.
I raised up prophets from among your sons and Nazirites from among your young men. Is this not so, people of Israel? declares the LORD.
But you made the Nazirites drink wine, and you commanded the prophets: Do not prophesy!
Now I will press you down where you stand, as a cart is pressed down when it is loaded with sheaves.
The swift will find no escape, the strong will not hold on to his strength, and the warrior will not save his life.
The archer will not stand his ground, the fleet of foot will not get away, and the horseman will not save his life.
Even the bravest of the warriors will flee naked on that day, declares the LORD.
